summary:
Allwork.Space republishes a Reuters wire report that Netflix plans to cut roughly 5% of its workforce, with an announcement possibly coming as early as the following week. The report originated with Puck News on Friday, citing people familiar with the matter. Netflix declined to comment.

Context given: Netflix's last major layoff round was in 2022, when it cut hundreds of jobs amid slowing growth and subscriber losses. The company had roughly 16,000 full-time employees at the end of last year.

The piece frames the reduction against an increasingly competitive streaming market, with media company consolidation and YouTube capturing a growing share of both viewership and advertising spend. Netflix has been diversifying beyond its core subscription business into advertising, live programming and gaming to broaden revenue sources.

The item is a short news brief with no workplace-operations angle: it does not discuss office attendance, hybrid policy, real estate, facilities, desk or room booking, or workplace technology. Reporting credited to Harshita Mary Varghese in Bengaluru, edited by Jonathan Ananda.
